title: 3.6 questions and comments
body:
**This issue is for quick questions or comments about tmux 3.6. Do not use this issue for bug reports, they will be ignored.** For bug reports please open a new issue with full information, see [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md).

**Note that it is very important to restart tmux entirely after upgrading.** This is particularly important with this release because one of the libraries that tmux uses changed its protocol. If you see this message when you try to attach it probably means you forgot to restart tmux:
~~~~
open terminal failed: not a terminal
~~~~

This release has many mostly small additions, improvements and bug fixes; the most significant changes are listed in [the 3.6 CHANGES file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmux/tmux/3.6/CHANGES). Many thanks to everyone who contributed and apologies to anyone who has been missed.

A few of the more notable changes are:

* Support for scrollbars (see the `pane-scrollbars` option), from Michael Grant. Michael has also contributed a number of other features, bug fixes and code improvements.

* Mode 2031 theme support, from Jonathan Slenders.

* Improvements to format operators (such as boolean expressions and `#?` from David Mandelberg and sorting for loop operators from Michael Grant) and new variables for buffers, sessions and cursor styles.

* Improvements to how tmux requests and reports information:
  - the ability send pixel size queries (from Dmitry Galchinsky);
  - forwarding of OSC 4 palette queries (prompted by a change offered by Tim Culverhouse);
  - support for reporting cursor, mouse, paste and focus state (from Andrea Alberti);
  - and querying of clipboard support (from James Holderness).

Note that as always due to limited time patch releases will only appear due to security issues or immediately obvious or showstopper bugs, so I encourage everyone to test the master branch ahead of the next release where they can.

The issue for the previous 3.5a release is [here](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/issues/4162) (now locked).

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: Looking at the [changes for 3.6](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmux/tmux/3.6/CHANGES) I see that the configuration options `prompt-cursor-colour` and `prompt-cursor-style` have been added. When configuring tmux with: ``` set-option -g message-style fg=green,bg=white set-option -g prompt-cursor-colour green ``` The cursor appears as a different shade of green than the message-style foreground, which I did not expect. What am I missing?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
It isn't possible to set cursor colour to an ANSI colour (except by querying its RGB value from the terminal which tmux does not do), so "green" for cursor colours is the default green which is RGB `#008000`.

If you want it to be the same colour as your terminal's ANSI green, you'll need to find out what that is as an RGB value and set it instead.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: That's helpful to know and an easy fix, thanks for the explanation.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Was the new COLORTERM-handling supposed to _actively unset_ the environment variables `COLORTERM`, `TERM`, `TERM_PROGRAM`, and `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION` during loading of config?

I use both `TERM` and `COLORTERM` in my `~/.tmux.conf` to make sure I set the right config, and suddenly both were unset after upgrading to 3.6, even though I actively set them in my environment.

From 29db8ac:
https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/29db8ac36eeefcb67eb87d80900b97eb515f2c80/environ.c#L260-L271 I don't really write C,  but it seems the new code  unsets the variables if `no_TERM` is true. The function is called from https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/29db8ac36eeefcb67eb87d80900b97eb515f2c80/job.c#L89-L94 where a comment states we should not set a new TERM while loading config. But not setting is not the same as unsetting, and if `TERM` is unset, we can no longer use it like the comment suggests. Though, I might be confused by double negatives and code I'm not familiar with :)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: What comment suggests what?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Oh yeah sorry for some reason that bit didn't show in the mail. You're right, we should probably not delete `TERM`.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
Hi,
On version 3.6 I'm getting incorrect output when I spawn a session with a custom path, and then immediately after I query the current path of the pane. I'm getting the current working directory instead of the path set during the creation of the session.

On 3.6 this returns the current directory I'm in, instead of /tmp:
```sh
tmux new-session -d -c /tmp; tmux display-message -p -F '#{pane_current_path}'
```
I tested the same thing on 3.5a the output is correct.

This is kind of a pain to deal with when scripting although of course a 'sleep 1' fixes this (in a not so elegant manner).

Would it be possible for tmux to maybe wait until a session is created before display-message targeted at that session is processed, or maybe for the new-session command to block until the session is fully up?

For a workaround is there a way to tell if a tmux session is fully up?

PS: If an issue should be created for this just let me know

comments.author: participant10
comments.body:
Got two questions:

1. after `set -g pane-scrollbars on`, the scrollbar doesn't show in TUI/alternate screen but will show in copy-mode. This makes the lines change when entering copy-mode from a TUI (e.g. lazygit, vim) because columns decreased due to the scrollbar, and each line now needs two lines to display. Is there a good way to avoid this?
2. What's the difference between the new `cursor-centre-vertical` command and `middle-line`?

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
```
set -g mode-keys vi
bind-key -T copy-mode-vi MouseDragEnd1Pane send-keys -X copy-selection -x
```
The above config for copy on mouse selection and drag stopped working on 3.6. Can confirm by downgrading to 3.5a.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant10 I don't think there is a way to avoid (1) as it is now... maybe we could make it not resize and instead truncate the lines, but it might be tricky... @participant12?

For (2) I don't think there is any difference, I forgot about `middle-line` and anyway it doesn't hurt having `cursor-centre-vertical` for symmetry with `cursor-centre-horizontal`.

comments.author: participant12
comments.body:
@participant10 @reporter When you enter the alternate screen, the scrollbar gets turned off.  When it's off, the pane is resized and reflowed so you get the extra column where the scrollbar was.  This is by design (nic and I discussed this when I did it).  It is definitely possible not to reflow and leave empty space where the scrollbar was when in the alt screen.  Should that be an option?  

It seems like you are talking about the reverse situation.  If I understand correctly, you are in alt-screen mode or scrollbar is in modal-mode where the scrollbar is off, you exit vi or enter copy-mode or something and the window reflows when it puts the scrollbar in, things wrap and where there was one (long) line, now you have two.  

I guess we could truncate the extra column but to be honest, it probably would be globally better have an option like above where you lose the scrollbar column (and padding) as usable screen area when in alt-screen mode, hence you never need to reflow the screen.  Frankly I would be concerned about truncating characters because it's destructive, you lose data.  To me this feels like it would be buggy.

To be clear if we create some option to reserve the scrollbar zone and you set scrollbar to `modal`, then in normal situations (not in a mode), you are going to be wasting screen realestate most of the time, there's going to be a blank area where the scrollbar would be but it's turned off.  Nic, please let me know if you want a new option for that and what it might be called and I'll add that to my todo list.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Well, neither choice seems ideal, either you lose a column in alternate screen (it is empty, or maybe better it shows a "full" scrollbar), or you lose access to the column when you enter copy mode. I don't really mind either way TBH...

comments.author: participant12
comments.body:
@participant10 Something I'm not quite clear on with what you are saying.  Could you please confirm if you are seeing lines wrapped when you exit alternate screen mode?  If so, can you provide me an example?  The thing is, I don't see this with alternate screen mode since the screen is saved and restored.  I haven't found a situation with `pane-scrollbars=on` where it adds extra lines that were not already there.

The only situation I have seen where you get extra lines is when `pane-scrollbars=modal` and you have a line that is exactly the screen width and you enter copy-mode or you start dragging with the mouse to copy some text.  Then, the scrollbar appears, the pane reflows, and only the long line gets wrapped to two lines.  This doesn't seem that bad.  If you truncate that line you wouldn't be able to copy it properly.  Could you please confirm if this is the situation you are seeing?

Does perhaps `tmux set pane-scrollbars modal` solve your issue?

I am ok to add an option to inhibit the behaviour of resizing the pane thus either the scrollbar area would appear full or empty in alternate screen mode.  But it's not clear to me if that would actually fix anything for you.

Instead of "truncating" the lines in copy-mode, it might be possible to "clip" to the visible region.  I believe I have seen such behaviour where a pane is wider than the layout and it does exactly this.  It lets you horizontally scroll by moving the cursor and it shifts things over and if I recall corretly puts a '$' at the end of lines which are clipped.  @participant15 am I misremembering this?  How would I cause this to happen?

comments.author: participant10
comments.body: @participant12 and @reporter thanks for taking a look > It seems like you are talking about the reverse situation Yes. I don't think `modal` or `on` makes a difference here, because either way the scroll bar is not visible in altscreen but visible in copy-mode. Maybe this would clarify: 1. empty tmux config, run `set -g pane-scrollbars on` 2. run `lazygit` (the screen shows lazygit with no scrollbar from tmux) 3. enter copy mode 4. the scrollbar appears, pushing lines like this I'd personally prefer the scrollbar to not appear if entering copy-mode from altscreen, since altscreen doesn't really scroll like normal situations. although i understand this may appear inconsistent. I didn't fully get the solution you were proposing, do you mean increase columns but also "unwrap" lines to let users scroll horizontally for one column? Also should i create a separate issue?

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
in 3.5a:

```
set -g status-left "#{?client_prefix,COMMAND,#[fg=#cdd9e5,bg=#347d39]text} "
```

print `text ` when no client prefix

in 3.6:

Print nothing.


original option that works fine in 3.5a:

```
set -g status-left "#{?client_prefix,#[fg=#cdd9e5]#[bg=#347d39] COMMAND,#{?pane_in_mode,#[fg=#cdd9e5]#[bg=#316dca] COPY,#{?synchronize-panes,#[fg=#cdd9e5]#[bg=#966600] SYNC,#[fg=#cdd9e5,bg=#347d39] 󰖲 #S}}} "
```

**Update**:

ok, the problem with `#[fg=#cdd9e5,bg=#347d39]` syntax in conditions. `#[fg=#cdd9e5]#[bg=#347d39]` print text
